content:
maria: Heads-up — priority customer ACME hit a p99 regression right after their billing window (~02:00 UTC). They report a spike from ~300ms to ~6-8s and a bunch of failures during the window. Paste of the customer-side symptoms below. Can eng take a look? :exclamation:

acme-support: seeing lots of 429 attach_throttle and intermittent 401 from auth at 02:01-02:05. Calls then queue up and latency climbs.

alex: I'm seeing the same in infra logs. Attach queue length jumped, autoscaler started scale-up but kept backing off due to attach_rate_limit. Also noticed this customer's Dedicated pool had min_size=0 (they rely on demand). Cold GPU warm starts + auth timeouts look correlated.

jordan: digging deeper — our attach broker returned 429s because attach attempts per-second exceeded the per-customer soft limit; at the same time auth-service returned 401 for ~20 requests (token refresh failed). If token refresh retries are blocking warmup, nodes never finish warmup and remain unavailable.

emily: can you paste the attach broker snippets?

alex: logs from attach-broker around 02:01:
```
[02:01:03] attach_request customer=acme req_id=7b9c status=queued queue_pos=1
[02:01:04] attach_request customer=acme req_id=7b9d status=rate_limited reason=attach_rate_limit
[02:01:05] attach_request customer=acme req_id=7b9e status=rate_limited reason=attach_rate_limit
[02:01:06] warmup_start node=node-xyz customer=acme req_id=7b9c
[02:01:07] warmup_error node=node-xyz err="auth:401" supplier=auth-service
[02:01:08] warmup_failed node=node-xyz reason=auth_failure
[02:01:09] attach_request customer=acme req_id=7b9f status=queued queue_pos=3
[02:01:10] autoscaler scaleup request queued pool=dedicated-acme reason=queue_depth=6
[02:01:11] autoscaler backoff pool=dedicated-acme reason=attach_rate_limit
```

maria: so two signals: (1) attach throttling limited concurrency, (2) auth 401s caused warmups to fail which prevented nodes from becoming available. Together => p99 blowup.

jordan: reproducer steps I used in staging (small script):
```bash
# simulate burst attach from customer account
for i in $(seq 1 120); do
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/attach -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"pool":"dedicated-acme","model":"redwood-7b"}' &
done
wait
```
Observed attach_rate_limit and then warmup failures when I intentionally revoked the token mid-burst to emulate a token refresh race.

alex: quick mitigations to get customer back to normal: 
- temporarily increase customer min_size to 1 or 2 so cold starts are reduced (min_pool change).
- bump attach soft limit for this customer for 30m to drain queue.
- enable prewarm (proactive warmup) for their dedicated pool.
- triage auth 401 root cause (token refresh job, KMS latency, or upstream provider).

maria: can eng-platform push the min_pool and prewarm toggle? We need an immediate stopgap before we dig into auth.

emily: @jordan @alex I can run the playbook — which exact config keys?

jordan: config ops commands (run from infra-admin):
```bash
# set min nodes to 2 for customer acme (ap-south region)
redwoodctl pools set --customer acme --pool dedicated --min-nodes 2 --region ap-south
# temporarily raise attach window for acme by 3x
redwoodctl limits set --customer acme --attach-rate 180
# enable prewarm for pool
redwoodctl pools prewarm enable --customer acme --pool dedicated --min-warm 1 --timeout 600s
```

alex: also patch suggestion: make our warmup flow treat auth 401s as transient for N=3 retries, and dont count transient auth failures as full warmup failure until after retries+backoff. That prevents a single KMS hiccup from killing warmup and leaving nodes unusable. Filing a follow-up PR.

emily: executing ops now, will monitor dashboards. tagging support to keep customer notified.

maria: FYI i've told customer we have mitigation in progress (increasing min_pool and enabling prewarm). Asking them to hold on failover. :thumbsup:

emily: deploy-bot: run result:
```
[02:10:05] redwoodctl: pools set --customer acme --min-nodes=2 -> succeeded
[02:10:06] redwoodctl: limits set --customer acme --attach-rate=180 -> succeeded
[02:10:07] redwoodctl: pools prewarm enable -> succeeded
```

deploy-bot: notification: config change applied for customer=acme by emily at 02:10:07 UTC

alex: monitoring metrics — attach queue length dropped, warmup success rate climbed from 40% -> 92% within 2 minutes. p99 trending down.

jordan: follow-ups:
- investigate auth-service token refresh spike at 02:01 (logs show a short window of elevated KMS latency).
- add circuit-breaker to warmup vs auth so we can fallback to a cached token path if KMS slow.
- consider per-customer soft attach burst windows or token jitter to avoid synchronized refresh storms.

maria: I've documented the incident in the customer ticket and scheduled a postmortem with ops + auth team at 16:00 UTC. Action items assigned: alex -> warmup retry PR, jordan -> auth dig + KMS traces, emily -> monitor + rollback plan.

emily: customer confirmed latency normalized and said thanks. Closing loop after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
